content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts show upward trend bias, failing to account for sharp downward corrections after spikes.
- Model underreacts to recent low prices; fails to adjust forecast downward when true values dip below recent history.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., post-90+ spikes), then gradually corrects — model lags in recognizing peak decay.
- Mean reversion is not captured: model holds high forecasts even when true values show clear downward drift.
- Forecasts are too smooth; fail to reflect volatility clustering or sudden reversals in price behavior.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are overly optimistic in early days, then gradually converge — but still lag behind true values by 1–3 days.
- Model ignores recent low points in history when forecasting; tends to anchor on recent highs instead.
